title: Release of the movie The Beastmaster
phrase: the release of the movie The Beastmaster
description: One of the pinnacle achievements of the sword and sorcery movie genre.

title: Release of the movie Conan the Barbarian
phrase: the release of the movie Conan the Barbarian
description: Not as good as The Beastmaster, but Conan the Barbarian earned lead actor Arnold Schwarzenegger worldwide recognition.

title: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
phrase: the Apollo 11 Moon landing
description: Apollo 11 (July 16–24, 1969) was the American spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon.

title: Wright brothers' first flight
phrase: the Wright brothers' first flight
description: The Wright Brothers did not solely rely on engine power to lift their flying machines off the ground. Instead, they emphasized the importance of piloting skills. Through over a thousand gliding flights from the top of Kill Devil Hill, the brothers were able to identify the engineering principles that allow for lift and the necessary controls to maintain an aircraft in flight.

title: Character Forrest Gump in the Vietnam War
phrase: Forrest Gump (the character) serving in the Vietnam War

title: Release of the movie Forrest Gump
phrase: the release of the movie Forrest Gump

title: Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) released in North America
phrase: the North American release of the NES
description: The NES ran at 60FPS… unless you had a bunch of sprites on the screen.

title: Super Nintendo Entertainment System (SNES) released in North America
phrase: the North American release of the Super Nintendo
description: No more hard angles on these controllers. And six action buttons!

title: Earliest known publicly demonstrated electronic game
phrase: the earliest known publicly demonstrated electronic game
description: The earliest known publicly demonstrated electronic game was created in 1950. Bertie the Brain was an arcade game of tic-tac-toe, built by Josef Kates for the 1950 Canadian National Exhibition.

title: Earliest videogame
phrase: the earliest videogame
description: "Tennis for Two" was the first videogame that was open to the general public. Prior games were entirely research projects or technology demonstrations. It was played on an oscilloscope which presented a side view of a tennis match. The custom built controller had a button to take a shot and a knob to adjust a shot's angle. Even this earliest videogame was very popular with long lines of people queuing up for a turn to play.

title: First clamshell laptop (GRiD Compass)
phrase: the first clamshell laptop (GRiD Compass)
description: The GRiD Compass was the first clamshell laptop. It weighed 10 pounds but is still considered the first truly portable laptop computer.

title: Gutenberg printing press introduced in Europe
phrase: Gutenberg's printing press being introduced in Europe
description: Around this time Johannes Gutenberg, of the German city of Mainz, introduced the printing press to Europe.

title: First movie ever recorded
phrase: the first movie ever recorded
description: An 11-frame clip of a man riding a horse. It was recorded by Eadweard Muybridge using 12 separate cameras that he designed to have a then cutting edge 1/25th of a second shutter speed. He also designed the zoöpraxiscope as a mechanism to view the photos as a movie.

title: Erlang programming language introduced
phrase: the introduction of the Erlang programming language
description: Developed and designed by Joe Armstrong, Erlang was originally proprietary to the Ericsson company. Erlang wasn't open sourced until years later in 1998. Erlang is fundamentally designed to be distributed, fault tolerant, soft realtime, and highly available. Erlang provides developer friendly concurrency abstractions, functional programming, and immutable data.

title: Erlang programming language open sourced
phrase: Erlang being open sourced
description: Jane Walerud is credited with the heroic effort of convincing Ericsson management that it was in everyone's best interest to open source Erlang and OTP. This was a monumental feat as the very term "open-source" had only even been coined a few months prior.

title: Elixir programming language introduced
phrase: the introduction of the Elixir programming language
description: In 2012 José Valim publicly introduced Elixir to the world as a new syntactically approachable language for the BEAM (Erlang's VM). Elixir has grown extremely popular in the years since and noted for its ease of use, scalability, and reliability.

title: JavaScript introduced
phrase: the introduction of JavaScript
description: In 1995 the Internet was a simpler place. Your browser client would make an HTTP request to a server and get a response back. Done and done. But the Netscape Communications Corporation wasn't satisfied. It wanted to bring interaction to the web. Interaction brought about by including a runtime in their browser to locally execute code sent from the web server. What could go wrong?

title: Node.js introduced
phrase: the introduction of Node.js
description: Long ago JavaScript was safely trapped within browser engines. Then everything changed when Google open sourced Chrome and developers used its JavaScript execution engine to build a server-side JavaScript runtime that we now call Node.js. Thus paving the way for the left-pad incident.

title: Left-pad incident
phrase: the left-pad incident
description: In 2016 a developer named Azer Koçulu unpublished more than 250 of his JavaScript packages from the npm registry, a popular package manager for the JavaScript programming language. One of the packages that was unpublished was a very small library called left-pad, which provided a simple function for padding a string with a specified character on the left side. The removal of the left-pad package caused a chain reaction, as many other packages that depended on it were also affected. This led to widespread disruption and caused numerous projects to break.

title: Ruby programming language introduced
phrase: the introduction of the Ruby programming language
description: Ruby is an interpreted, high-level, scripting language with a strong foundation in object oriented programming and famously expressive syntax. In the words of creator Yukihiro Matsumoto: "I really wanted a genuine object-oriented, easy-to-use scripting language. I looked for but couldn't find one. So I decided to make it."

title: Python programming language introduced
phrase: the introduction of the Python programming language
description: Introduced in 1991 by Guido van Rossum. Python was designed to have a small core, large standard library, and to be easily extensible via modules. That foundational design has kept Python popular in the decades since.

title: Infocom released Zork I
phrase: the release of Zork I
description: Arguably the most famous work of interactive fiction and a huge financial success for Infocom. In 2007, Zork was noted by the Library of Congress as one of the ten most important video games of all time.

title: Rocket League released
phrase: the release of Rocket League
description: Soccer. With cars. That are also rockets. A simple game with a simple premise and simple controls that ends up having a surprisingly deep skill well with innovative mechanics still being discovered even years later.

title: Lucasarts released The Secret of Monkey Island
phrase: the release of The Secret of Monkey Island
description: One of the foundational works of point and click gaming. Frustrated with the "gotcha!" deaths and unwinnable states of contemporary adventure games, creators Ron Gilbert and Tim Schafer designed Monkey Island so that it was always possible to win. A design choice that continued through the rest of Lucasarts adventure games.

title: Origin Systems released Wing Commander
phrase: the release of Wing Commander
description: A landmark game in the space combat genre by Chris Roberts who is now working to create Star Citizen.

title: Interstellar movie released
phrase: the release of the movie Interstellar
description: Interstellar is a 2014 science fiction film directed by Christopher Nolan and starring Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, and Michael Caine. The film follows a group of astronauts who travel through a wormhole in search of a new home for humanity, as Earth is on the verge of environmental collapse. The story is based on scientific concepts such as relativity and gravity, and explores human themes of love and sacrifice.

title: Titanic sinks
phrase: the sinking of the Titanic
description: The Titanic was equipped with a number of innovative features, including electricity, elevators, and a swimming pool. It also had a gym, a Turkish bath, and a squash court. Its historic sinking is still one of the deadliest maritime disasters in history.

title: Titanic movie released
phrase: the release of the movie Titanic
description: It's hard to overstate how much of a media phenomenon Titanic was during its theatrical release. One interesting fact is that the set crew built a 1:1 scale replica of the Titanic's Grand Staircase for the production.

title: Louisiana Purchase
phrase: the Louisiana Purchase
description: The purchase doubled the size of the United States and was considered a major accomplishment of the presidency of Thomas Jefferson. The Louisiana Purchase was made possible by the Napoleonic Wars, which had left France in need of funds and weakened its hold on its North American colonies. In 1803, the United States offered to purchase New Orleans and the land west of the Mississippi River for $10 million, but France instead offered to sell all of the Louisiana Territory, which included a much larger area, for $15 million. France, though, controlled only a small part of it. Most of the land was home to Native Americans, so for most of it the United States really bought the right to take it from them by treaty or by conquest.

title: Linux first released
phrase: the first release of Linux
description: Linus Torvalds started developing Linux as a personal project while he was a student at the University of Helsinki in Finland. He released the first version of Linux, called version 0.01, on September 17, 1991. Since then, Linux has become one of the most widely used operating systems in the world, powering everything from servers and supercomputers to smartphones and embedded devices.

title: Back to the Future movie release
phrase: the release of the movie Back to the Future
description: Marty McFly is accidentally sent back in time to 1955 in a time-traveling DeLorean car built by Doc Brown. He meets his parents as teenagers and must ensure that they fall in love in order to return to his own time.

title: Back to the Future Part II movie release
phrase: the release of the movie Back to the Future Part II
description: In this sequel, Marty and Doc travel to the future, specifically to the year 2015. Their goal is to prevent Marty's future son from making a terrible mistake but then they must travel back to 1955 to fix a destructive alteration to the timeline.

title: Back to the Future Part III movie release
phrase: the release of the movie Back to the Future Part III
description: In the final movie of the trilogy, Marty must travel back in time to the Wild West and the year 1885. Marty must help Doc Brown, who became stranded in 1885 during the events of Back to the Future II.

title: Marty McFly is stuck in 1955 during Back to the Future
phrase: Marty McFly being stuck in 1955
description: 1.21 gigawatts! A bolt of lightning!

title: The "future" in Back to the Future Part II
phrase: the "future" of Back to the Future Part II
description: Hoverboards don't work on water, unless you've got POWER!

title: Marty and Doc in the Wild West during Back to the Future Part III
phrase: Marty and Doc in the Wild West in Back to the Future Part III
description: Mr. Fusion powers the time circuits and the flux capacitor. But the internal combustion engine runs on ordinary gasoline, it always has. There's not going to be a gas station around here until sometime in the next century. Without gasoline, we can't get the DeLorean up to 88 miles per hour.

title: The Lord of the Rings movie release
phrase: the release of the movie The Lord of the Rings
description: Ralph Bakshi's ambitious undertaking which brought Middle Earth to life via cel animation and rotoscoped live action footage.

title: The Fellowship of the Ring movie release
phrase: the release of the movie The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
description: Achieving near-universal critical acclaim is no small feat. The first of Peter Jackson's LOTR trilogy succeeds.

title: The Two Towers movie release
phrase: the release of the movie The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
description: The opening scene of Gandalf fighting the Balrog is cinematic legend. We can almost forgive the movie's strange and complex divergence from the plot of the book which requires characters to make strangely illogical decisions in order to keep the story lined up for the third movie.

title: The Return of the King movie release
phrase: the release of the movie The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
description: Sadly this movie misses a major point of the books by not including the scouring of the Shire. More than a battle set piece the hobbits reclaiming the Shire from an authoritarian government is a critical balance to the quest to destroy the ring.

title: The Fellowship of the Ring book release
phrase: the release of the book The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
description: "Don't adventures ever have an end? I suppose not. Someone else always has to carry on the story."

title: The Two Towers book release
phrase: the release of the book The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
description: "I would not take this thing, if it lay by the highway. Not were Minas Tirith falling in ruin and I alone could save her, so, using the weapon of the Dark Lord for her good and my glory. No, I do not wish for such triumphs, Frodo." —Faramir. The book version of Faramir was far more level headed and wise.

title: The Return of the King book release
phrase: the release of the book The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
description: Unlike the movies, the books contain the critically and thematically important "scouring of the Shire" which contextualizes the effects of the larger adventure. Frodo, Sam, Merry, and Pippin return to the Shire to find it under the control of an authoritarian regime that has torn down the old houses and replaced the mill with machinery that pollutes the air and water. They inspire and lead an uprising to overthrow those in power and restore the Shire. If you've only ever seen the movies, you should at least read this section of the books.

title: The Dark Side of the Moon album release
phrase: the release of the album The Dark Side of the Moon
description: If you don't already know what this is then you should hear this album at least once. Or at least watch a Polyphonic episode about the album on YouTube.

title: Walt Disney Company founded
phrase: the founding of The Walt Disney Company
description: Founded by Roy and Walt Disney, at the time it was called the Disney Brothers Studio. It wasn't until 1928 with Steamboat Willie that the studio really started to take off.

title: AOL Instant Messenger released
phrase: the release of AOL Instant Messenger
description: On May 1, 1997 AOL Instant Messenger (AIM) was released. It wasn't the first way to chat with friends online (ICQ) but it was extremely popular.

title: AOL Instant Messenger shut down
phrase: the shutdown of AOL Instant Messenger
description: In 2017 Verizon (having acquired AOL in 2015) discontinued AIM as a service after years of declining use. For years users had been moving to even easier to use services such as Google Chat and iMessage.

title: Launch of Sputnik 1
phrase: the launch of Sputnik 1
description: Earth's first artificial satellite was a polished metal ball about the size of a beach ball that pretty much just orbited and beeped. But radio operators around the world could hear that beep, and it kicked off the Space Race.

title: Yuri Gagarin's flight into space
phrase: Yuri Gagarin becoming the first person in space
description: Vostok 1 made a single orbit of Earth in 108 minutes. Gagarin didn't land with his capsule: he ejected about 7 km up and parachuted down on his own!

title: Launch of Voyager 2
phrase: the launch of Voyager 2
description: Despite the name, Voyager 2 launched first. It's still the only spacecraft to have visited Uranus and Neptune.

title: Launch of Voyager 1
phrase: the launch of Voyager 1
description: Launched sixteen days after its twin on a faster path, Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object. It carries a golden record of sounds and music from Earth.

title: First Space Shuttle launch
phrase: the first Space Shuttle launch
description: STS-1 sent Columbia into orbit twenty years to the day after Yuri Gagarin's flight. It was the first time Americans had flown in space since 1975.

title: Space Shuttle Challenger disaster
phrase: the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster
description: Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after launch, killing all seven crew members. An O-ring seal in one of the solid rocket boosters failed in the unusually cold weather. The Challenger disaster is still a foundational case study of engineering safety, group communication, and management.

title: Launch of the Hubble Space Telescope
phrase: the launch of the Hubble Space Telescope
description: Hubble's first images were blurry because its main mirror had been ground to slightly the wrong shape. A 1993 shuttle mission fitted it with corrective optics. I always thought it was cool that a telescope had to get glasses.

title: Mars Pathfinder landing
phrase: the Mars Pathfinder landing
description: Pathfinder bounced onto Mars wrapped in airbags, then let out Sojourner, the first rover to drive on another planet.

title: First crew arrives at the International Space Station
phrase: the first crew arriving at the International Space Station
description: Expedition 1 started a continuous human presence in space that hasn't been broken since.

title: Curiosity rover lands on Mars
phrase: the Curiosity rover landing on Mars
description: Curiosity was too heavy for the bounce down on airbags approach, so NASA lowered it to the surface on cables from a rocket-powered sky crane. The engineers called the landing "seven minutes of terror."

title: New Horizons flies past Pluto
phrase: New Horizons flying past Pluto
description: New Horizons launched in January 2006, when Pluto was still a planet, and took nine and a half years to get there.

title: Launch of the James Webb Space Telescope
phrase: the launch of the James Webb Space Telescope
description: Launched on Christmas morning, folded origami-style to fit inside its rocket. On the way out to its orbit a million miles from Earth, it had to unfold a sunshield the size of a tennis court and it worked perfectly.

title: First message sent over ARPANET
phrase: the first message sent over ARPANET
description: A student at UCLA tried to log in to a computer at the Stanford Research Institute by typing "LOGIN." The system crashed after "LO."

title: First email sent between computers
phrase: the first email sent between two computers
description: Ray Tomlinson sent it over ARPANET and chose the @ sign to separate the user from the machine. He later said he couldn't remember what the message said, probably something like QWERTYUIOP.

title: Apple II goes on sale
phrase: the Apple II going on sale
description: Steve Wozniak's design, with color graphics and eight expansion slots, turned Apple into a real company. VisiCalc, the first spreadsheet program, gave people a reason to buy one for the office.

title: IBM announces the IBM PC
phrase: IBM announcing the IBM PC
description: IBM built it from off-the-shelf parts and licensed its operating system from a small company called Microsoft. That made it easy to clone, and the clones are why we still say "PC."

title: Release of the Macintosh
phrase: the release of the original Macintosh
description: Announced by the "1984" Super Bowl ad two days earlier, the Macintosh brought the mouse and a graphical interface to people who couldn't afford Apple's Lisa.

title: Tim Berners-Lee proposes the World Wide Web
phrase: Tim Berners-Lee's proposal for the World Wide Web
description: His manager at CERN, Mike Sendall, called it "vague, but exciting." Berners-Lee has given the date as March 12, but he admits the document itself only says "March 1989" and that March 12 is actually his mother's birthday.

title: The World Wide Web goes public
phrase: the World Wide Web going public
description: Tim Berners-Lee posted a short summary of the project to the alt.hypertext newsgroup and invited anyone interested to join in.

title: Release of Windows 95
phrase: the release of Windows 95
description: Microsoft licensed "Start Me Up" by the Rolling Stones to introduce the Start button, and people lined up at midnight to buy an operating system.

title: Founding of Google
phrase: the founding of Google
description: Larry Page and Sergey Brin incorporated Google while they were PhD students at Stanford. Its first office was their friend Susan Wojcicki's garage.

title: Wikipedia launches
phrase: the launch of Wikipedia
description: Wikipedia started as a side project to feed draft articles into Nupedia, an encyclopedia written by experts. It quickly outgrew Nupedia, which shut down in 2003.

title: Apple introduces the iPod
phrase: Apple introducing the iPod
description: "1,000 songs in your pocket." The first iPod had a scroll wheel that actually turned, and at first it only worked with Macs.

title: Launch of Facebook
phrase: the launch of Facebook
description: It launched as TheFacebook, and at first only Harvard students could sign up.

title: First video uploaded to YouTube
phrase: the first video uploaded to YouTube
description: "Me at the zoo" is 19 seconds of co-founder Jawed Karim standing in front of the elephants at the San Diego Zoo. The cool thing about them is that they have really, really, really long trunks.

title: Twitter launches to the public
phrase: Twitter launching to the public
description: Its original code name was twttr, inspired by Flickr and the five-character length of American SMS short codes. Posts were limited to 140 characters until 2017.

title: Release of the iPhone
phrase: the release of the original iPhone
description: No App Store, no 3G, no copy and paste. All Apple offered was a compelling and intuitive user experience.

title: Bitcoin's genesis block
phrase: the mining of Bitcoin's first block
description: Satoshi Nakamoto put a newspaper headline into the very first block: "The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks."

title: Release of the song Summer of '69
phrase: the release of the song "Summer of '69"
description: Bryan Adams released "Summer of '69" as a single on Memorial Day 1985. Critics pointed out he was only nine that summer.

title: The summer of 1969
phrase: the summer of 1969
description: The summer of 1969 had the Stonewall riots, the Apollo 11 Moon landing, and Woodstock.

title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
phrase: the assassination of Julius Caesar
description: On the Ides of March, a group of senators stabbed Caesar to death during a session of the Senate. They meant to save the Republic, but the civil wars that followed ended with his heir Octavian ruling Rome alone as Augustus.

title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
phrase: the fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: The Germanic king Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus, the last emperor in the West, and sent the imperial regalia off to the emperor in Constantinople. The Eastern half of the empire carried on for nearly another thousand years.

title: Magna Carta
phrase: the sealing of Magna Carta
description: Rebel barons forced King John of England to agree to it at Runnymede. Neither side kept its promises and the pope annulled it within months, but the idea that even the king is bound by the law outlived them all.

title: Fall of Constantinople
phrase: the fall of Constantinople
description: The Ottoman sultan Mehmed II took the city after a 53-day siege, ending the Byzantine Empire, the last piece of the Roman Empire still standing.

title: Martin Luther's Ninety-five Theses
phrase: Martin Luther's Ninety-five Theses
description: Luther's objections to the sale of indulgences spread across Germany and kicked off the Protestant Reformation. He's famously said to have nailed them to a church door in Wittenberg, but that part may be legend.

title: Adoption of the Declaration of Independence
phrase: the adoption of the Declaration of Independence
description: The Continental Congress voted for independence on July 2 and approved Thomas Jefferson's declaration two days later. To keep South Carolina and Georgia on board, Congress cut Jefferson's passage blaming King George III for forcing slavery onto the colonies.

title: Signing of the US Constitution
phrase: the signing of the US Constitution
description: Thirty-nine delegates signed it at the end of the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia. It protected slavery, partly through the Three-Fifths Compromise, which let states count three-fifths of their enslaved people toward their seats in Congress. It's the oldest written national constitution still in force.

title: Storming of the Bastille
phrase: the storming of the Bastille
description: Parisians stormed the fortress looking for gunpowder and found only seven prisoners inside. It became the symbol of the French Revolution, and July 14 is still France's national day.

title: Battle of Waterloo
phrase: the Battle of Waterloo
description: Wellington's and Blücher's armies ended Napoleon's return from exile for good. This time he was sent to Saint Helena, a remote island in the South Atlantic, where he died in 1821.

title: Emancipation Proclamation
phrase: the Emancipation Proclamation
description: Lincoln's order declared enslaved people in the rebelling Confederate states free, but it depended on the Union army to enforce it. Federal troops announced it in Galveston, Texas, on June 19, 1865, the day now celebrated as Juneteenth.

title: Assassination of Abraham Lincoln
phrase: the assassination of Abraham Lincoln
description: John Wilkes Booth shot Lincoln at Ford's Theatre five days after Lee's surrender at Appomattox. Lincoln died the next morning, the first US president to be assassinated.

title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
phrase: the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
description: The archduke's driver took a wrong turn in Sarajevo and stalled the car while backing up, right next to Gavrilo Princip. Within weeks the shooting had pulled most of Europe into World War I.

title: Armistice ends World War I
phrase: the armistice that ended World War I
description: The fighting stopped at 11 a.m.: the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month. Many countries still mark the day as Armistice Day, Remembrance Day, or Veterans Day.

title: Nineteenth Amendment ratified
phrase: the ratification of the Nineteenth Amendment
description: Tennessee's vote put it over the top after Harry Burn, the youngest member of the state legislature, changed his vote because his mother wrote him a letter asking him to. The amendment barred states from denying anyone the vote on the basis of sex.

title: Black Tuesday stock market crash
phrase: the Black Tuesday stock market crash
description: Some 16.4 million shares changed hands in the worst day of the Wall Street crash, which led into the Great Depression.

title: Germany invades Poland
phrase: Germany invading Poland
description: Britain and France declared war on Germany two days later, starting World War II in Europe.

title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
phrase: the attack on Pearl Harbor
description: Japan's surprise attack on the US Pacific Fleet in Hawaii brought the United States into World War II. Franklin Roosevelt called it "a date which will live in infamy."

title: D-Day
phrase: D-Day
description: The Allied landings in Normandy are still the largest seaborne invasion in history, with nearly 5,000 landing and assault craft.

title: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima
phrase: the atomic bombing of Hiroshima
description: The first nuclear weapon used in war. The United States bombed Nagasaki three days later, and Japan announced its surrender on August 15.

title: Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech
phrase: Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech
description: King gave it to more than 250,000 people at the Lincoln Memorial during the March on Washington. The famous part wasn't in his prepared text: Mahalia Jackson shouted "Tell 'em about the dream, Martin!" and he improvised it.

title: Assassination of John F. Kennedy
phrase: the assassination of John F. Kennedy
description: Lee Harvey Oswald shot Kennedy from the Texas School Book Depository as his motorcade passed through Dallas. Two days later Jack Ruby shot Oswald on live television.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
phrase: the fall of the Berlin Wall
description: At a press conference, East German official Günter Schabowski mistakenly announced that new travel rules took effect immediately. Crowds rushed the checkpoints that night and the guards let them through.

title: Nelson Mandela released from prison
phrase: Nelson Mandela's release from prison
description: Mandela had spent 27 years in prison, much of it on Robben Island. Four years later he became South Africa's first Black president.

title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
phrase: the dissolution of the Soviet Union
description: Mikhail Gorbachev resigned on Christmas Day and handed the nuclear launch codes to Boris Yeltsin. The next day the Soviet Union formally ceased to exist.

title: First recorded Olympic Games
phrase: the first recorded Olympic Games
description: Tradition says the only event was the stadion, a sprint the length of the stadium, and that the first champion was Coroebus of Elis.

title: Legendary founding of Rome
phrase: the legendary founding of Rome
description: The Romans said Romulus founded the city on April 21 after a fatal falling-out with his twin brother Remus. Rome still celebrates its birthday on April 21.

title: Colosseum opens
phrase: the opening of the Colosseum
description: Emperor Titus opened it with inaugural games that reportedly included flooding the arena for a show of swimming horses and bulls. It could hold an estimated 50,000 to 80,000 spectators.

title: Shakespeare's Globe Theatre opens
phrase: the opening of Shakespeare's Globe Theatre
description: Shakespeare's company took their old playhouse apart beam by beam and used the timber to build the Globe. It burned down in 1613 during a performance of Henry VIII.

title: Boston Tea Party
phrase: the Boston Tea Party
description: Sons of Liberty, some dressed as Mohawk warriors, spent three hours dumping more than 340 chests of East India Company tea into Boston Harbor.

title: Discovery of the Rosetta Stone
phrase: the discovery of the Rosetta Stone
description: French soldiers found it while rebuilding a fort in Egypt. It has the same decree in Greek, Demotic, and hieroglyphs, which helped Jean-François Champollion crack hieroglyphs in 1822. When the British defeated the French in Egypt they took the stone to London, where it has been in the British Museum since 1802. Egypt's former antiquities chief Zahi Hawass has repeatedly demanded it back.

title: Lewis and Clark set out
phrase: Lewis and Clark setting out on their expedition
description: The Corps of Discovery headed up the Missouri River to explore the newly bought Louisiana Territory, picking up Sacagawea as an interpreter along the way, and reached the Pacific in 1805. Part of the job was telling the Native nations they met that their lands now belonged to the United States.

title: Gold found at Sutter's Mill
phrase: the discovery of gold at Sutter's Mill
description: James W. Marshall spotted gold while building a sawmill in Coloma, California. The news brought about 300,000 people to California in the gold rush that followed. For Native Californians it was a catastrophe: mining poisoned rivers and destroyed habitats, and disease, starvation, and violence sped up the collapse of their population.

title: First Pony Express ride
phrase: the first Pony Express ride
description: Relay riders carried mail between Missouri and California in about 10 days, which many said was impossible. The transcontinental telegraph put it out of business after just 18 months.

title: Golden spike completes the transcontinental railroad
phrase: the driving of the golden spike
description: Leland Stanford drove the ceremonial last spike at Promontory Summit, Utah, joining the Central Pacific and Union Pacific railroads into one line across the country. Chinese workers did most of the heavy labor on the Central Pacific, and eight of them laid its last rail.

title: Brooklyn Bridge opens
phrase: the opening of the Brooklyn Bridge
description: Not everyone trusted it at first, so the next year P. T. Barnum had Jumbo lead a parade of 21 elephants across to show it was safe.

title: Statue of Liberty dedicated
phrase: the dedication of the Statue of Liberty
description: A gift from the people of France, built in France and shipped over in crates. It started out shiny and reddish-brown, and within twenty years its copper had weathered to green. The statue's left foot steps on a broken chain and shackle, for the abolition of slavery after the Civil War.

title: Eiffel Tower completed
phrase: the completion of the Eiffel Tower
description: Gustave Eiffel celebrated by leading officials up the stairs to the top. It was meant to be temporary and was slated for dismantling in 1909, but it turned out to be useful as a radio tower.

title: First modern Olympic Games
phrase: the first modern Olympic Games
description: About 241 athletes from 14 nations competed in Athens. The highlight for the hosts was the marathon, won by Greek water carrier Spyridon Louis.

title: First Nobel Prizes awarded
phrase: the first Nobel Prizes being awarded
description: Awarded on the fifth anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death. The story goes that the inventor of dynamite funded the prizes after a newspaper mistakenly ran his obituary under the headline "The merchant of death is dead."

title: Mona Lisa stolen from the Louvre
phrase: the theft of the Mona Lisa
description: Vincenzo Peruggia, a glazier who had worked at the Louvre, simply walked out with it.

title: Amundsen reaches the South Pole
phrase: Roald Amundsen reaching the South Pole
description: Amundsen's Norwegian team got there five weeks ahead of Robert Falcon Scott's British party.

title: Panama Canal opens
phrase: the opening of the Panama Canal
description: The cargo ship SS Ancon made the first official passage. Ships between the Atlantic and the Pacific no longer had to go all the way around South America. It cost thousands of lives to dig. An estimated 22,000 people died from disease and accidents during the earlier French attempt alone.

title: Discovery of Tutankhamun's tomb
phrase: the discovery of Tutankhamun's tomb
description: A worker on Howard Carter's dig uncovered a step cut into the rock. When Carter first peered inside, he was asked if he could see anything: "Yes, wonderful things."

title: Lindbergh flies solo across the Atlantic
phrase: Charles Lindbergh's solo flight across the Atlantic
description: Lindbergh landed in Paris 33 and a half hours after taking off from New York, winning the $25,000 Orteig Prize.

title: Golden Gate Bridge opens
phrase: the opening of the Golden Gate Bridge
description: It had the longest suspension bridge span in the world until 1964. The Navy wanted it painted in black and yellow stripes, but it got International Orange instead.

title: Discovery of the Lascaux cave paintings
phrase: the discovery of the Lascaux cave paintings
description: 18-year-old Marcel Ravidat found the entrance when his dog went poking into a hole left by an uprooted tree. The paintings inside are around 17,000 to 22,000 years old.

title: Mount Rushmore completed
phrase: the completion of Mount Rushmore
description: The Lakota call the mountain Tȟuŋkášila Šákpe Pahá, Six Grandfathers Mountain. The 1868 Treaty of Fort Laramie recognized the Black Hills as Lakota land, but the United States broke it as prospectors moved in and took the land in the 1870s. Fifty years later, four presidents' faces were carved into the mountain. In 1980 the Supreme Court ruled that the Sioux were owed compensation, but they have refused the money and still demand the land back.

title: First ascent of Mount Everest
phrase: the first ascent of Mount Everest
description: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the summit. By coincidence, the news broke in London on the morning of Queen Elizabeth II's coronation.

title: Disneyland opens
phrase: the opening of Disneyland
description: Opening day went so badly that it became known as "Black Sunday."

title: Discovery of the Terracotta Army
phrase: the discovery of the Terracotta Army
description: Farmers near Xi'an dug into the tomb complex of China's first emperor. The pits hold an estimated 8,000 soldiers, most of them still buried.

title: Infocom released Deadline
phrase: the release of Deadline
description: Infocom's first mystery. You're a detective called to a Connecticut estate to look into a suspicious death while the suspects go about their own business, and you can't make an arrest stick without motive, method, and opportunity. The box came with a police file and three white pills in a plastic bag, which started Infocom's tradition of feelies.

title: Infocom released Planetfall
phrase: the release of Planetfall
description: Steve Meretzky's first game. You're an Ensign Seventh Class who mops the decks until the ship blows up. On the planet below you meet Floyd, a childlike robot who became Infocom's most popular character, and plenty of players have told Meretzky they cried over what happens to him.

title: Infocom released Enchanter
phrase: the release of Enchanter
description: Originally meant to be Zork IV. You're a novice Enchanter sent after an evil warlock in the hope that he won't take you seriously. Spells have to be memorized before they're cast, and each one is a nonsense word the parser treats as a verb, so FROTZ BOOK makes the book glow.

title: Infocom released The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
phrase: the release of the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy game
description: Designed by Douglas Adams himself with Steve Meretzky, and famously devious. Getting the Babel Fish out of its dispenser takes a Rube Goldberg chain of obscure items, and failing it leaves the game unwinnable. Infocom sold T-shirts that said "I got the Babel Fish!"

title: Infocom released A Mind Forever Voyaging
phrase: the release of A Mind Forever Voyaging
description: You play PRISM, an artificial intelligence sent decades into the future of a simulated South Dakota town to report on what a sweeping set of conservative policies will do to it. Steve Meretzky wrote it out of dismay at Ronald Reagan's 1984 re-election. It didn't sell, but critics loved it, and some now call it prescient.

title: Infocom released Trinity
phrase: the release of Trinity
description: Brian Moriarty's prose poem about the atomic bomb opens with a Soviet missile on its way to Kensington Gardens, sends you through test sites and Nagasaki just before each detonation, and ends in the New Mexico desert on July 16, 1945. Widely regarded as one of Infocom's best, it was the last game Infocom released while it was still solvent.

title: Infocom released Leather Goddesses of Phobos
phrase: the release of Leather Goddesses of Phobos
description: Infocom's first "sex farce," with a naughtiness setting that runs from tame to suggestive to lewd, like G, PG, and R. Steve Meretzky said he was hoping to get it banned from 7-Eleven. Tom Clancy named it one of his favorite computer games.

title: Activision shut down Infocom
phrase: Activision shutting down Infocom
description: MIT staff and students founded Infocom in 1979. It sank much of its game money into Cornerstone, a business database, and after Cornerstone failed it laid off half its staff and sold itself to Activision in 1986. Activision closed it three years later.

title: Lucasfilm Games released Maniac Mansion
phrase: the release of Maniac Mansion
description: Ron Gilbert didn't like typing commands, so he built a point-and-click interface and an engine called SCUMM to run it, and SCUMM went on to power Lucasarts adventure games for years. You can put the hamster in the microwave. The NES version had to be heavily reworked because Nintendo of America thought the game was inappropriate for children.

title: Lucasfilm Games released Zak McKracken and the Alien Mindbenders
phrase: the release of Zak McKracken and the Alien Mindbenders
description: The second SCUMM game. Zak, a writer for a tabloid, has to stop the aliens who've taken over The Phone Company from making everyone on Earth dumber with a 60 Hz hum.

title: Lucasfilm Games released Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade: The Graphic Adventure
phrase: the release of the Last Crusade graphic adventure
description: Released alongside the movie, with a replica of Henry Jones' Grail diary in the box. Its "Indy Quotient" score carried over between games, and the only way to max it out was to find every alternate solution, like fighting a guard instead of slipping past him.

title: Lucasfilm Games released Loom
phrase: the release of Loom
description: Led by Brian Moriarty, who came over from Infocom after writing Trinity. Loom drops the verb list entirely: Bobbin Threadbare casts spells by playing four-note drafts on his distaff, and some work in reverse, so Dye played backwards becomes Bleach.

title: Lucasarts released Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge
phrase: the release of Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge
description: The first game with iMUSE, Lucasarts' adaptive music engine, which shifts the music smoothly as the story moves along. A critical success but a commercial disappointment, it ended on a cliffhanger that Ron Gilbert didn't pick back up until Return to Monkey Island in 2022.

title: Lucasarts released Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis
phrase: the release of Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis
description: Indy and Sophia Hapgood, an archaeologist turned psychic, race the Nazis to Atlantis. Early on you pick the Team, Wits, or Fists path, and each has its own puzzles, scenes, and places to visit.

title: Lucasarts released Day of the Tentacle
phrase: the release of Day of the Tentacle
description: The sequel to Maniac Mansion. Bernard, Hoagie, and Laverne are scattered across time trying to stop Purple Tentacle from taking over the world. The whole original Maniac Mansion is playable on a computer inside the game, which no game had done before.

title: Lucasarts released Sam & Max Hit the Road
phrase: the release of Sam & Max Hit the Road
description: Steve Purcell's Freelance Police, a dog and a "hyperkinetic rabbity thing," chase a bigfoot missing from a carnival across America's tourist traps. It was one of the first games with full voice acting.

title: Lucasarts released Full Throttle
phrase: the release of Full Throttle
description: Tim Schafer's first game as project lead. Biker Ben has to clear his name after he's framed for murder. It swapped the verb list for a pie menu and hired professional voice actors, including Mark Hamill as the villain.

title: Lucasarts released Grim Fandango
phrase: the release of Grim Fandango
description: Manny Calavera is a travel agent for the newly dead, working off a debt in a Land of the Dead that mixes the Aztec afterlife with 1950s film noir. Often listed among the greatest games ever made, it was a commercial failure that helped end Lucasarts' adventure games.

title: Nintendo founded
phrase: the founding of Nintendo
description: Fusajiro Yamauchi founded Nintendo in Kyoto to make handmade hanafuda playing cards, which sold well in the city's yakuza-run gambling parlors. Nobody knows for sure what the name was meant to mean, not even Yamauchi's descendants.

title: Nintendo released the first Game & Watch
phrase: the release of the first Game & Watch
description: Gunpei Yokoi got the idea on a bullet train, watching a bored businessman poke at a pocket calculator. Each handheld played a single game on a calculator-style LCD, and the line ran until 1991.

title: Nintendo released Donkey Kong
phrase: the release of Donkey Kong
description: Built to use up unsold Radar Scope arcade cabinets, and handed to a first-time designer named Shigeru Miyamoto. Its hero, a carpenter who climbs a construction site to rescue Pauline, was later called Jumpman, and then Mario.

title: Nintendo released the Family Computer (Famicom) in Japan
phrase: the Japanese release of the Famicom
description: Hiroshi Yamauchi asked for a simple, cheap console that could play arcade games from cartridges, and Masayuki Uemura designed it. Yamauchi saw it as a home computer disguised as a toy, and some at Nintendo called it "Yamauchi's Trojan Horse."

title: The video game crash of 1983
phrase: the video game crash of 1983
description: Home video game revenue in North America fell almost 97% between 1983 and 1985, and analysts wondered whether video games had a future at all. The industry recovered a few years later, mostly thanks to the NES.

title: Nintendo released Super Mario Bros.
phrase: the release of Super Mario Bros
description: Shigeru Miyamoto wanted a more colorful platform game with a scrolling screen and bigger characters. Add the Super Mushroom, the Fire Flower, and the Starman, and you get one of the best-selling games ever, with more than 58 million copies sold.

title: R.O.B. arrived with the NES Deluxe Set
phrase: R.O.B. arriving with the NES
description: After the crash of 1983, American stores didn't want video games. So Nintendo of America built its launch around a toy robot, to sell the NES as a sophisticated electronic toy. R.O.B. only ever worked with two games, Gyromite and Stack-Up, but he got the NES onto store shelves.

title: Nintendo released The Legend of Zelda
phrase: the release of The Legend of Zelda
description: Link starts with nothing but a small shield until an old man in a cave hands him a sword: "It's dangerous to go alone!" The US version was one of the first games with an internal battery for saving.

title: Nintendo released Metroid
phrase: the release of Metroid
description: Samus Aran hunts Space Pirates through the caverns of Zebes, and in the best endings takes off the suit to reveal she's a woman, at a time when women in games were mostly queens or kidnapped princesses. Those endings went to the fastest players, which made it an early speedrunning favorite.

title: Nintendo released Super Mario Bros. 3
phrase: the release of Super Mario Bros. 3
description: The Super Leaf and the Tanooki Suit let Mario fly. Many Americans first saw it in the final scene of the 1989 movie The Wizard, and it sold more than 17 million copies.

title: Game Boy released in North America
phrase: the North American release of the Game Boy
description: Gunpei Yokoi's team picked price, battery life, and durability over a color screen and a fast processor. In North America it came with Tetris, and its color competitors were stuck with poor battery life.

title: Mattel released the Power Glove for the NES
phrase: the release of the Power Glove
description: In The Wizard, Lucas Barton plays Rad Racer with one. Everyone else found the controls imprecise and hard to use, and it cost $100, with only two games made for it.

title: Nintendo 64 released in North America
phrase: the North American release of the Nintendo 64
description: Its controller was the first with a thumbstick as standard, and the console had four controller ports for multiplayer. Nintendo even delayed its launch to avoid angering retailers "in the same way Sega had."

title: Nintendo released Super Mario 64
phrase: the release of Super Mario 64
description: Mario's first 3D game. Shigeru Miyamoto came up with the idea while making Star Fox, and the team built the camera system first.

title: Nintendo released The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
phrase: the release of Ocarina of Time
description: It introduced Z-targeting, which locks Link onto an enemy, along with Navi the fairy to explain it. It's still the highest-rated game on Metacritic, at 99 out of 100.

title: Wii released in North America
phrase: the North American release of the Wii
description: Wii Sports came in the box and became the killer app, and the motion-sensing Wii Remote sent Microsoft and Sony off to build Kinect and PlayStation Move. More than 101 million sold.

title: Nintendo Switch released
phrase: the release of the Nintendo Switch
description: A tablet that docks to the TV or goes with you, with Joy-Con that split into two controllers. More than 155 million shipped, making it Nintendo's best-selling console.

title: Sega released the SG-1000 in Japan
phrase: the release of the Sega SG-1000
description: Sega's first home console came out the very same day as Nintendo's Famicom. It beat Sega's sales projections, helped by a Famicom recall over a faulty circuit. Then Nintendo fixed the circuit. In Taiwan it was popular for a while, until cheaper Famicom clones took over, so Sega lost to Nintendo's knockoffs too.

title: Sega Master System released in North America
phrase: the North American release of the Sega Master System
description: The rare Sega console with better hardware than its Nintendo rival. It didn't help: Nintendo's licensing rules kept third-party games exclusive to the NES, so the Master System's library was smaller, and the NES dominated North America anyway.

title: Sega Genesis released in North America
phrase: the North American release of the Sega Genesis
description: It could show 61 colors at once from a palette of 512, while the Super Nintendo picked from 32,768. The controller had three main buttons until 1993, when Sega added three more for fighting games like Street Fighter II. So Sega's marketing promised "blast processing," an obscure graphics programming method nobody actually used. In fairness, Sonic helped it outsell the SNES for four Christmases in a row.

title: Sega Game Gear released in North America
phrase: the North American release of the Game Gear
description: Its full-color backlit screen beat the Game Boy's monochrome one. It also ate six AA batteries every three to five hours, so the Game Boy kept playing while the Game Gear went back to the store for more.

title: Sega CD released in North America
phrase: the North American release of the Sega CD
description: A CD drive for the Genesis with room for full-motion video, which its limited color palette gave what Digital Pictures' founder called "a horrible grainy look." One of those grainy games, Night Trap, ended up at the center of Congress's hearings on video game violence. Nintendo canceled its own CD add-on, dodging a grainy bullet.

title: Sega 32X released in North America
phrase: the North American release of the Sega 32X
description: An add-on to make the Genesis more powerful, which needed its own power supply, a cable to link it to the Genesis, and another conversion cable for the original model. Sega was launching the Saturn in Japan at the same time, so developers and buyers skipped it, and it was discontinued in 1996.

title: Sega Saturn released in North America
phrase: the North American release of the Sega Saturn
description: Sega surprise-launched it at the first E3, four months early, for $399. Retailers who weren't told were upset, and KB Toys refused to carry it at all. Inside were two CPUs and eight processors in all, a complex design that got it little third-party support. The Nintendo 64 outsold it.

title: Sega Dreamcast released in North America
phrase: the North American release of the Dreamcast
description: "9/9/99 for $199." It was the first console with a built-in modem for online play and is remembered as ahead of its time. It was also Sega's last console: Sega discontinued it in March 2001 and became a third-party developer.

title: Namco released Pac-Man
phrase: the release of Pac-Man
description: Toru Iwatani wanted a game that would appeal to women as well as men, when most games were about war or sports. In Japan it was Puck Man, and it was renamed for North America out of fear of what vandals would do to the P.

title: Alexey Pajitnov created Tetris
phrase: the creation of Tetris
description: Alexey Pajitnov made it in his spare time at a Soviet state computing center, so he couldn't sell it for profit. Western companies sold the rights to each other for years, and the Soviet licensing agency licensed it to Nintendo for the Game Boy. The rights only went back to Pajitnov at the end of 1995.

title: Origin Systems released Autoduel
phrase: the release of Autoduel
description: Steve Jackson Games' Car Wars as an open-road RPG. Win some money at amateur night in the arena, then build your own car, from the power plant to the mine-layers, oil slicks, rockets, and flame throwers. Then run courier jobs between the towns of the Atlantic seaboard. In 2018 Steve Jackson asked for the source code so it could be republished. There's still no other game quite like it.

title: Electronic Arts released Mail Order Monsters
phrase: the release of Mail Order Monsters
description: Create a monster, arm it with modern and futuristic weapons, buy it tentacles so it can handle the fancier weapons, and send it to fight a friend or a horde of computer opponents. Your monster saved to disk and got stronger as it won, which has gotten it called a precursor to Pokémon. Many happy childhood hours went into this one. It was wild to have dinosaurs firing tactical nuclear weapons at each other!

title: Release of the movie Tron
phrase: the release of the movie Tron
description: Jeff Bridges plays a programmer and video game developer who gets pulled inside a mainframe and has to fight his way out, Light Cycles and all. It was one of the first films to make extensive use of computer animation, though only fifteen to twenty minutes of it. It wasn't even nominated for the visual effects Oscar, and director Steven Lisberger guessed the Academy thought he'd "cheated by using computers."

title: Release of the movie Tron: Legacy
phrase: the release of the movie Tron: Legacy
description: Twenty years after Kevin Flynn vanished, his son Sam follows a pager message from Flynn's shuttered arcade onto the Grid. Its villain Clu looks like the Bridges of 1982: a stand-in's head was replaced with a digitally de-aged young Bridges. Daft Punk scored it and cameo as disc jockey programs.

title: Release of the movie The Last Starfighter
phrase: the release of the movie The Last Starfighter
description: Alex Rogan beats the high score on the Starfighter arcade game at his trailer park, which turns out to be a recruiting test for an alien defense force. Instead of models, its spaceships were 3D-rendered on a Cray X-MP supercomputer, 27 minutes of effects in all. The end credits promise a real Starfighter arcade game from Atari, but Atari dropped it after seeing the film and deciding it wouldn't be a hit.

title: Release of the movie Top Gun
phrase: the release of the movie Top Gun
description: Maverick and Goose get sent to the Navy's Fighter Weapons School after the pilot ahead of them loses his nerve. Paramount paid as much as $7,800 an hour for fuel and operating costs whenever the Navy's jets flew for the film, and the Navy set up recruiting booths in some theaters. It was the highest-grossing film of 1986, and "Take My Breath Away" won the Oscar.

title: Release of the movie Top Gun: Maverick
phrase: the release of the movie Top Gun: Maverick
description: More than thirty years later Maverick is still a captain, sent back to Top Gun to train a class that includes Goose's son, Rooster. Tom Cruise put the cast through a three-month boot camp so they could fly in the back seats of real Super Hornets with IMAX cameras in the cockpit. Its stunts and then COVID-19 pushed it back nearly three years, and it grossed $1.5 billion, the most of Cruise's career. It was Val Kilmer's final film role.
